prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and policies in the Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 (non-ideological)

Economy, tax and pensions
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate both State Pension and a new age-related personal allowance by the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5%; maintain current pension tax rules and pensioner benefits.
- Raise at least £6bn a year tackling tax avoidance/evasion.

Business, regulation and innovation
- Maintain full expensing and consider extending it to leasing when affordable; no rise in corporation tax.
- SME plan: business rates changes, VAT threshold smoothing, Open Finance, explore Regional Mutual Banks, lighter reporting, prompt payment enforcement, retain key investment reliefs, £250m Invest in Women Fund, SME-focused procurement.
- Public R&D to £22bn/yr; £1.5bn for AI compute; £4.5bn for strategic manufacturing; expand Catapults.

Infrastructure, transport and planning
- Reallocate £36bn from HS2 to regional transport: roads, rail (Northern Powerhouse Rail section; Midlands Rail Hub), £8.3bn potholes, more bus routes; 85% gigabit by 2025, nationwide by 2030; nationwide 5G standalone.
- Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; expand open access; nationwide contactless pay-as-you-go.
- Backing Drivers Bill: ban road pricing, reverse London ULEZ expansion, local referendums for LTNs/20mph; extend £2 bus fare cap for whole Parliament.
- Speed up major infrastructure approvals; reduce meritless judicial reviews.

Energy and net zero
- Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; maintain windfall tax to 2028-29 (with investment allowances); new gas plants.
- Treble offshore wind; launch CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; progress Wylfa nuclear.
- Keep energy price cap; reform standing charges; Pumpwatch; £6bn for home efficiency and a national voucher scheme; support onshore wind with local consent; protect best agricultural land from solar; retain fracking moratorium.
- Ensure household green levies lower than 2023; review Climate Change Committee remit to consider costs/security.

Welfare, work and migration
- Reform disability benefits (PIP) and tighten work capability assessments from Sept 2025; overhaul fit notes via specialist assessors; tougher sanctions after 12 months; complete Universal Credit rollout; new Fraud Bill.
- Legal cap on work and family visas, falling annually; monthly Rwanda removal flights; process asylum claims in six months; increase visa fees and health surcharge; pre‑travel health checks; higher skilled salary thresholds retained.

Families, childcare and education
- 30 hours free childcare from nine months to school start by Sept 2025; wraparound care by Sept 2026.
- Child Benefit moved to household basis, tapering between £120k–£160k income.
- Ban mobile phones in school day; Advanced British Standard for 16–19; two hours PE weekly; expand teacher bonuses; 60,000 more SEND places and 15 special free schools; parents’ right to see teaching materials.
- Mandatory National Service at 18: 1‑year competitive paid military/cyber option or 25 days civic service.
- Create 100,000 more apprenticeships by closing poor‑outcome degree courses; implement Lifelong Learning Entitlement.

Health and social care
- NHS spending to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgery builds/modernisations; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
- Dental Recovery Plan (2.5m extra appointments), new contract, require new dentists to serve in NHS for a period.
- Patient choice across NHS, charity and independent providers; £3.4bn for NHS tech (App as single front door, AI, imaging, FDP); reduce 5,500 managers; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health actions; expand mental health support (school teams to 100% coverage by 2030; early support hubs nationwide).

Policing, justice and public safety
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; facial recognition and other tools; Martyn’s Law; hotspot policing and tougher community sentencing; tougher sentences for serious crimes; four new prisons; more removals of foreign offenders; protest-related powers.

Housing and planning
- 1.6m homes; end nutrient neutrality rules with mitigation fees to unlock 100k homes; fast-track brownfield in 20 largest cities; raise London densities; urban development corporations; protect Green Belt.
- First-time buyer Stamp Duty threshold £425k made permanent; new Help to Buy (up to 20% equity loan, 5% deposit); continue Mortgage Guarantee.
- Leasehold reform (cap ground rents to £250 then peppercorn; end misuse of forfeiture); Renters Reform Bill to end Section 21 with court reforms; temporary CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; controls on holiday lets.

Defence and foreign policy
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn for munitions; Defence Innovation Agency (5% R&D + 2% exploitation); long‑term Ukraine support; veterans’ legislation and benefits; national resilience plan.
- Maintain global partnerships; return to 0.7% ODA when fiscal conditions allow.

Rural, farming, fisheries and environment
- Increase UK farming budget by £1bn over Parliament; legally binding food security target and Index; 50% public food spend local or higher‑standard; fast‑track farm infrastructure; tapered seasonal worker visas; replicate £100m UK Seafood Fund.
- Maintain record flood defence funding; Plan for Water (stronger penalties, river recovery network, 100% overflow monitoring); extend SW £50 rebate; new National Park; tree/peat commitments; tougher waste crime penalties; limit new incinerators.

Law and equality
- Clarify Equality Act that “sex” means biological sex; single legal sex; implement Cass Review; ban private prescription of puberty blockers; protect single‑sex wards and intimate care.

Union and devolution
- Comparable UK-wide public service data; protect internal market; Intertrade UK; extend Shared Prosperity Fund and town funds to devolved nations; specific investments and transport/energy projects in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; implement Windsor Framework and legacy measures.
